name: [CANCELLED] Puzzle Creek
description:
UPDATE: Unfortunately several issues have arisen and we are unable to walk on Sunday. We hope to reschedule in the near future.

Puzzle Creek is a club classic walk area. This version will be the one day walk starting from upper Puzzle Falls, follow the creek to Puzzle Falls and Thunderbolt junction, down to St Peter’s Gate falls, and cross into Running River Gorge.  Wonderful creek and gorge scenery. 

RATED – HARD 

A long rock hop walk point to point, no track, some sand walking, all up about 9 hrs walking. No major hill climbs. Good stamina required. 

REQUIRED
- Water: minimum 4 lt water, refill from creek (recommend water treatment / filter for refills). 
- Food for the whole day. 
- Usual day walk gear, including good footwear for rock hopping
 - Sun protection. 

MEET – 7 am in Paluma (location available on registration). There is an option to stay overnight Saturday in Paluma -please ask.

Estimate back in Paluma around 6 pm, so back in Townsville about 8 pm. 

COST 
Non-members $5 fee. 

Must be over 18years to participate 
 

WALK LEADER, INFO and REGISTRATION  

To nominate and more info, contact leader - Wilfred directly or message the FB page. 
Our email address won't be monitored as frequently over the next couple of weeks.

name: [FULL] Short, Sweet and Social: Elliot Springs and breakfast
description:
SATURDAY 29 AUGUST 

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED: Easy
Start the weekend off with an easy on-track walk of approximately 5k.

DESCRIPTION
We'll start from Wadda Mooli Park at Elliot Springs and climb the track up the ridge before returning the same way. Being only a short walk, we'll be down in time for a BYO breakfast or coffee and catch up before heading home. The walk should take approx 1.5hrs depending on the speed of the group.

FITNESS
This walk is suitable for most people people.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for 2hrs eg 1-2L
- Clothing: comfortable
- Enclosed footwear
- Food + beverages for breakfast after (optional)
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.
- Dogs are allowed on leash

Non members = $5 walk fee

name: Wallaman Falls / Stoney Creek (Pls read event description)
description:
SUNDAY 23 August – Wallaman Falls / Stoney Creek 
 
RATED – HARD
 
Stoney Creek. Starting at Wallaman Falls. We will walk down the track to the base of the falls. After taking in the views, we will start rock hopping down the creek. If we come to a cliff, we will turn around and return via the same route. Swimming in water pools.

An off-track rock hop walk returning to the starting point. There is no track except for the start, mostly rock hopping. Bring shoes that grip on granite rocks. Rocks may be wet and slippery. 

WHAT TO BRING:
- minimum 3 lt water, refill from creek (recommend water treatment / filter for refills)
- Food for the day
- Usual day walk gear, including good footwear for rock hopping
- Sun protection. 

WHEN + WHERE:
Meet – 8 am at Wallaman Falls. Or camp at Wallaman Falls on Saturday night.

Estimated back at cars by 4pm.

COST 
Non-members $5 fee. 

FOR MORE INFO OR REGISTRATION
Must be over 18years to participate 
Leader Luen.

name: Cape Cleveland weekend
description:
CAPE CLEVELAND WEEKEND
Option 1: FRIDAY 14/9 - SUNDAY 16/9 
Option 2: SATURDAY 15/9 - SUNDAY 16/9

REGISTRATION IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE DETAILS BELOW. FULL WALK DETAILS ARE AVAILABLE  ON ENQUIRY OR REGISTRATION - please see below.

RATED: Hard
The walk will be entirely offtrack.  It is a long hot walk with some steep climbs,all cross country, long grass, uneven footings. You will need good fitness and be known to the walk leader.

THE PLAN:
Our plan is to walk out to Cape Cleveland (groups departing both Friday 14/8 and Saturday 15/8) for the weekend, returning Sunday 16/8 via a different route. 

We'll walk out to the cape carrying only our day packs.  Enroute we'll have great views over the Cape, Townsville and Maggie Is. If we're lucky we may even spot a whale!  

Participants are required to provide all their equipment and be self sufficient.  Camping gear and food will be transported to the Cape by boat (see below for cost). You must be available to drop off your gear on Thursday afternoon and pick up on Monday afternoon.

WHAT TO BRING:
- Camping gear - you must be self sufficient
 - Water: you will need water for full day eg minimum 5L. There is no resupply during the day. Water is available at the Cape.
 - Clothing: there is a lot of long grass and scrub so full long sleeve clothing is recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves. Warm clothing for night time and recommended to be carried during the day.
 - Enclosed footwear
 - Food for the days
 - Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
 - Usual bushwalking gear 
 - Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.
- Waterproofing of gear going on the boat is highly recommended
 
COST
 Non members = $5 walk fee for insurance
 Barge cost = $40 pp for gear transport and camping access
 Must be over 18years to participate
 
WALK LEADER, INFO and REGISTRATION
 Walk organiser is Wilfred.
 To discuss suitability, to register or for more information please contact tsvbush@hotmail.com and we will get back to you asap, or contact Wilfred directly.
 
WALK DETAILS
 Meet time: 0700 departure both days from Alligator Creek
 Return time: plan to be back at cars by 1700 Sunday
Gear drop off: Thursday 4-6pm (Oonoomba)
Gear pick up: Monday 4-6pm (Oonoomba)

name: Lower Little Crystal Creek Falls - Introductory
description:
SUNDAY 9 AUGUST - Lower Little Crystal Creek Falls
Introduction to creek based and offtrack walking

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

DESCRIPTION
An introductory walk to explore the lower reaches of Little Crystal Creek. There is no track - this walk will be all cross country - including a steep scrubby hill, and some rock hopping followed by long grass, some more scrub to bash through with uneven footing (there has been burn-off in the area, so hopefully not too much long grass / scrub). This walk Includes a ravine / gorge explore, and a great waterfall and pool for a swim. This is a good introduction to the type of off track cross country walking the TBWC does. 

FITNESS
It is not a long distance, but reasonable off-track fitness is required for the steep hill climb and rock hopping.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for half day eg minimum 2L
- Clothing: there is a lot of long grass and scrub so full long sleeve clothing is recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed footwear
- Food for the day
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Usual bushwalking gear 
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.

WALK DETAILS
Meet time: 8am Bruce Hwy near Paluma turnoff
Return time: aim to be back at the cars by lunchtime

name: Castle Rock + Paradise Beach (pls read event details)
description:
SUNDAY 2 AUGUST - Castle Rock + Paradise Beach

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED: 
MEDIUM HARD - long grass, some scrub, three hills, beach walking

DESCRIPTION
This is a great coastal day walk on Cape Cleveland. We are taking a different route to normal so the first 2 km is exploratory as we bash our way through long grass and scrub, vines etc (all that fun stuff).
In the gullies we may encounter a lot of Blue Tiger butterflies.
There are three steep hills. Two along the route between beaches (following rough steep tracks), and the final steep climb to Castle Rock (no track). To clamber on top of Castle Rock, for the best beach view, is superb (the rock summit does challenge some though, especially if windy). 
Lunch will either be at Castle Rock or down on Paradise Beach.  There will be opportunity for swim at the beach.

WALK DETAILS
Meet time: 7:30am at Alligator Ck (location will be given on registration).
Return time: Back at the cars 5-6pm

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for full day eg minimum 4L. There is no resupply during the day.
- Clothing: there is a lot of long grass and scrub so full long sleeve clothing is recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed footwear
- Food for the day

name: FULL Wongaloo Wetlands
description:
EVENT FULL
SATURDAY 1 August (afternoon) - Wongaloo Wetlands introductory nature explore

This will be a short explore of Wongaloo Wetlands Conservation Park (Cromarty). Although it will be short it distance it will be 4 hrs duration as the primary focus will be wildlife spotting and photography.  The area is a prolific wetlands bird area so hopefully we'll see many brolga, Jabiru, magpie geese plus much more. 
Apart from wetlands there are woodlands and a bit of rainforest on the reserve which we may also explore if it's not too wet after the rain last week.

So if you like wetlands and birds +/- photography, this is a good opportunity to observe. This will be a small group event.

MEETING TIME & PLACE:
Please contact Keith for exact details.  Likely start time will be around 1-2pm. Duration is approx 4 hours.

WHAT TO BRING:
- You need water/food for 4 hrs
 - clothing: suggest long clothing / gaiters due to some bush / long grass. No bright clothing please!
- Insect repellent highly recommended. 
- cameras with telephoto reach (if available + optional)
- the most important thing you need is patience

name: Ross River Paddle
description:
Ross River Paddle - 1 August 2020

Calling all paddlers. Join us for a leisurely cruise up the Ross River. The plan is to launch from Loam Island and paddle upstream for 1-1.5hrs before returning. BYO vessel and gear.

WHEN: Saturday 1 August, ready for a 7:15am departure. We plan to back by 10:30am.

WHERE: Loam Island (BOAT RAMP). There is ample parking here but please park out of the way of cars with boat trailers.

WHAT TO BRING:
A ‘seaworthy’ kayak/canoe + related gear (eg paddle, gloves, PFD if required)
Water + food
Sun protective clothing and hat
Sunscreen, insect repellent
Waterproofing for anything that needs to stay dry
Shoes suitable to get wet for entry/exit 
Container to collect rubbish (optional)

FACILITIES: There is a toilet located close by, picnic tables

COST:
Visitors/non members = $5 

WHO:
Anyone who would like to come. Beginners welcome if you have access to a kayak/canoe. This is planned to be a social paced paddle to explore some of the river. If you would like a fast paddle please consider if this event is right of you. We will keep together in a rough group.

Must be 18yrs or over to participate.

REGISTRATION OR MORE INFO:
Please email the club tsvbush@hotmail.com or message the FB page for organiser (Katherine) contact details. 

For the the privacy of activity leaders, contact details and some locations won’t be published on Facebook.

Numbers will be limited to promote the safety and enjoyment of all and to reduce our environmental impact. 

Due to COVID-19, please do not attend if you are unwell. Social distancing and hygiene practices are strongly encouraged.
